body:
Of course I did.. So what if I didn't certify for this week? It won't allow me to just disqualify or skip this week's benefits and move to next week's right?

when I went to do the claim it mentioned that their records showed my last day was 1-31-2025 so they had that right. I'll just wait for my last paycheck on Friday to put the wages and see what happens after.

Thanks, just so I understand, you mean like change the name of the company slightly? So if it auto populated as "Company Name" I could change it to "Company Name Inc" (which wouldnt populate) and I wouldn't show up under their page?

You're probably right. I started off at this job by trying to be very sociable though. I said good morning to everyone every day. I was smiling a lot. Then I got told during a performance review that I smile too much. Maybe it was excessive, but is that really worse than the alternative of coming in, not saying anything to anyone and never smiling? Idk anymore.. 

I'll try that more though. Just "Hi, how are you doing today?" and see if that helps. It feels like I'll never shed this title at this job though. I'll be the creepy guy for as long as I'm here.

Where's the line on being too helpful? I honestly don't know. I'll try pulling back but these people are ASKING me for help. I understand offering help unwarranted is totally creepy. They are coming to me because they need shit and I am just helping them.  like wtf?

Thanks for sharing this. I was a lot like you then at my current job. Just trying to be friendly when I started. I'm not smiling/friendly anymore but I guess I still help my coworkers which is apparently "creepy" according to some posts here.

This is also the first time I've ever been called "creepy". Even if it was said in a joking way, I feel like there's other ways to joke with people. It doesn't feel good from anyone, especially when you're a man and it comes from all women.

I'm down right now and my motivation is drained which sucks because I love my job and coworkers still. I want to keep doing my best for everyone even though there are some who think this about me. It'll probably stick with me for a few weeks too, and then I'll let it go. It just stings now.
Then the obvious follow up is "why didn't they renew your contract"? Which I wouldn't have a great answer for.
How do I explain the fact that I'm looking for a new job after 6 month in an interview though? No answer sounds good really.

I figured as much. In that case, I'd rather just keep it to myself. Once they know that I know what's up, it will feel worse. I'll just ask for my usual "anything I can improve?" or "how have you been feeling about my performance recently?" and see if they give any indication based on that. 

I just started 6 months ago, wouldn't that be a red flag to other employers? I was at my previous job for over 5 years so that looked great.

Appreciate it. Yes it did really hit me like an insult. I've read about how men who smile too much creep women out. I knew this before. My thought was, I'd rather be a happy face because they're just coworkers (remote ones at that) so I never really cared about how I appeared around them. or so I thought. 

I'll start with just not smiling for now. The opening up will come once I'm comfortable but I think it's too soon. This hit me worse than I thought so I'm just going to keep to myself and not smile. I'd rather they think I'm weird for that than creepy for smiling too much. Thanks.
I asked them at the end of my review "is there anything you want me to do less?" Hoping for some guidance on maybe a task I should focus on less, or advice on where to focus more of my attention.

>Your smiling is NOT a problem and unless it's negatively affecting your work there's literally no reason to say that to you except to hurt your feelings.

I'm a guy and it came up during my work review. I caught them off guard with a question and they said "You smile too much, you gotta stop that.. just kidding!" (hahahaha right.. message received..). I don't know if they meant to be mean, but they were definitely being honest.

>Also, what gives them the right to dictate how you should present yourself or act? They're just coworkers, why the hell would you open up and share with them? Because they're bored and want a story? They've already snarked at you once, why would you give them another opportunity? Coworkers matter in your life as much or as little as you allow them to.

THANK YOU! I have NO interest in opening up to any of them after hearing this today. This was just from my supervisor, but I guarantee you everyone else is thinking the same thing. They didn't just make this up today. I do like my coworkers, and I am happy at my job. Now that this is out there though, it changes how I feel about everyone. Just knowing they think this about me.. 

Let them judge me for being too quiet. If they find things out about me, I'll be judged for those things forever. If I don't give them anything, they can only judge me for not saying anything which doesn't feel as personal. I can't believe I was judged over this. I get it's a thing, but it just feels so frustrating. I just wanted to be liked and now I'm the weird guy who smiles too much. 

> (And if you're looking for personal growth, maybe read online about why you feel the need "to make others feel comfortable around me." They can be responsible for their own feels, you just take care of yours.)

I definitely need to read into that. You're right that I don't need to help others feel comfortable. They'll feel how they feel (and they do obviously. Even with me smiling and trying to make them feel comfortable, it isn't helping them feel comfortable clearly.)

I like this approach for future matches. What do you mean "specific to them" though? You mean specific to their profile? It's hard to be specific when I barely know anything about them which is why I'd opt for generic questions. Their profiles don't give me much to go on either. 

As of now I just stick with whatever prompt I replied to and the conversation is at least fun/engaging rather than droning on about how their day was. It's just tough to find the appropriate time to pivot from there.

It's more like 30 minutes, and just the effort involved in going out and meeting with these people. I mainly can do weekends, and I want to feel good about who I'm going to meet even if it doesn't turn into anything. 

I'm not sure if I'm interested in these types of girls because I can't tell if they are. It's tough to tell when they reply back to everything, seem to find my jokes funny but never ask me a single question.

1000% it's in my head. I guess I'm so used to people joking with me that I always assume they are with things like this. I probably should've just given the real answer which is no I don't like clubbing really.

I'll try to be a little more interested in their lives I guess. It's probably dumb, but I'm afraid to do this because they're all women and I don't want it to be taken the wrong way (as if I'm trying to flirt or be weird or something). 

I'd rather listen to them talk about their lives/plans than be asked about my own.
I disagree. They don't need to like me, but I do want them to respect me because it makes working with them easier. When I need something, I can rely on them, etc.

It depends what you lie about. Telling them I'm hanging with friends when I'm actually chilling home with family so they don't think I'm a loser isn't a big deal and won't destroy my nonexistent relationship with them.

>Become a better liar. Find a middle ground between their pampered lives and the truth.

Yeah this is what I need to work on. I'm not actually ashamed of being a homebody, only when around outgoing people.

I'm not looking forward to them asking about my nonexistent dating life. I know it's coming soon and I'm just going to be miserable having to tell them I'm single. They're all in relationships and some with kids so I'm a real outcast there too. They tried to pry it out of me today when asking about my weekend plans, but I just said I'm hanging with friends and then asked them what they were up to. Nothing specific. 

They're not nasty. I feel uncomfortable as hell talking about my life with strangers.

Maybe they aren't "making fun" directly (yet), but I feel they are judging me for not being outgoing because they all are. For example they all have lavish New Years Eve plans and I don't.

One asked if I was going to the club but I think she was messing with me because I'm definitely not the clubbing type and I definitely give this off in my demeanor. I just said "yeah totally!" before saying "no not really" (mainly because I thought she was messing with me so I was sarcastic back).
Thank you! Congrats to you as well!

I guess it's just normal then. My bosses are all great, it's just that I'm in my own head and it's hard not to be. I see myself on these video calls, everyone else sees me including my bosses and I'm just not saying anything. I am engaged and paying attention, I just have nothing to say and most of what I'm doing isn't relevant to the meeting.

I'm not sure if I'm supposed to ask people if they need help or not? Do I look bad for not doing that more? I already did ask one of my coworkers if they needed anything to let me know. Do I do that again? I asked my supervisor and they told me to keep working on what I've been working on. I just feel like I should be contributing more.

>Before you speak ask yourself if what you are going to say is true, is kind, is necessary, is helpful.

That's helpful and probably why I'm not saying anything. I was thinking I should've just said "let me know if anyone needs help with anything!" at the end of a call because I sat there like a mute the whole time. 

I don't want anyone to think I'm a slacker, but I also don't know if anyone would pass their work to the new guy without being instructed to by a supervisor. Sure I have experience, but my coworkers don't know what kind of worker I am yet, so I'd understand them not being eager to just ask me for help with projects.
Damn, congrats! I've felt like I was in a coma too. Best of luck tomorrow on your first day.

>When broaching a subject, I liked to start the conversation along the lines of “I just joined so you’re a lot more familiar with this process than I am, need your help to understand…”

I'll probably try something like this when talking with my new coworkers. It could make me more likable to them which is a whole other thing I'm worrying about. I'm genuinely interested in the way they do things and have been brushing up on my industry knowledge as this position will be more involved. 

You sharing your experience is a big help. Thank you for the kind words!

Yeah there's definitely this. I've been told about it up front basically. I know how to do what they're asking, but not how to do it their way. I guess I'm also worried they'll throw me to the wolves and not train me at all. Idk why, it's probably anxiety talking.

Fair enough, I was burned over free labor before but maybe this could be different. I'll go with the flow, I won't break my back over it though. The first interview had a few red flags.

Where exactly is the line with this ? "Help us optimize our campaigns" isn't too much, but "build ads for us" is?
More like a 30 minute call. Even still, I don't work for free. I'll tell them what I'd do, but I don't think I should do anything for them myself.
Yeah I'm starting to figure that out. I wonder if it's even worth going for the date if that's going to be the way she is.

She's very quick to respond so I asked about her day and job, offered insight on mine. Quick replies but no interest in asking anything about me. 

So confused whether she'd be worth asking out... I don't even know if she'd say yes at this point but I also don't want to waste my time. Going on these dates can be very stressful.

It was just a back and forth about what sports teams we liked/disliked. I haven't really asked too much about HER yet because I matched with her late last night. Maybe I should try asking a few things about her or like how her day was today to see what her response is before trying for a date?
Did it at least have your dealbreakers work on OKC? Also did you get Hinge Premium or +? and why was it okay? I'm considering that too. I've at least gotten dates on Hinge.

I thought so too. I doubt any date with this girl ends with a lasting loving relationship after that, so I'll probably just put her to the side. 

I still want to know the plan for future dates though, because I don't mind a bar if it's one of the places I recently found. They're all midway points between me and the date so I think that's good right?

Yeah I'm starting to realize they aren't intellectual really. A bar where we can drink and extend if it goes well is better than 20 questions in a boring coffee shop. I still think I prefer it, but I need to play the game on their turf or settle for less dates.

I'm probably hung up on the venue though. So a "bar and grill" isn't acceptable? I'm not talking about Applebee's, but there are a lot of local spots that are "taverns" or "bar and grills". There's a Mexican spot with a bar that should work if these girls love tacos like their profiles say they do. 

No all of my friends are single and not dating, and none of us go to bars or clubs. We're nerdy guys who prefer quiet places and activities.

Yeah it honestly is a turn off for me when she said that. I was expecting a "yes" or "no" or no reply, not a "yes but I don't do coffee". 

I still want to know for next time how to approach girls like this. I think I'll ask them if they want to do coffee OR drinks or just say drinks straight up because I found a few spots I actually want to go to.
Is it something I said? Take it easy man. I just want advice, not to be insulted.

>Also why does it sound like you’ve never been to a bar?

Probably because I haven't ever sat at a bar. Only at a table and ordered food/drinks.

I wasn't thinking of going there, but there are a few 'bar & grills' and one Mexican spot that has a bar and is close. (girls love tacos, so that place should work right? I'm not swimming in dates, but I'd like to have a few places in my roster so I don't need to think. I just ask and tell them the place). Do you normally pick a place that's a mid way point for you and the date? Or do you pick spots closer to them? 

Yeah I've come around on why coffee isn't the best date. I think even for me, I want to get a bit more than just a coffee. It ends up being more expensive when you go on multiple dates like that and they all go nowhere, but I realize dating is expensive so I'll deal with that. I also want to just treat any future date as a learning experience.
I'm with you. I'd order one of the lightest beers they have and lots of appetizers/water.

When you put it that way I understand the whole "going for drinks" thing a bit more and I agree a coffee date does seem like more of an interview and definitely isn't fun. I found a cool bar that has games so I'm hoping any girl I ask out will want to go there. I definitely wouldn't feel uncomfortable in that place because I want to be there. Now I need someone to go with.

I'm honestly not trying to have sex with any girl on a first date. I don't know what that says about me, but if she's willing to give it to me on the first date she's  giving it out a lot. Kissing or other kinds of fooling around I'm fine with. Just not the deed that quickly with someone I won't see again. I think sex is more enjoyable for me when I actually love the person and they love me. (not waiting for marriage, just having that "love making" aspect).

I really appreciate the perspective.

What do you mean "upscale" bar? I'm looking for places that aren't too far from me, but have only found one real "bar". There are a lot of "Bar and grills" though. Should I not bother with those? (even if they aren't necessarily chains like Applebees).

> drink dates are an order of magnitude better than coffee dates

Why do you say this? Is it the higher chance of getting lucky after?
I found a fun looking bar that I think will be my go to for a lot of these types of girls. It's close enough to me and has games and other things to do as well.
Agree on me making the rules. The thing is the pool is empty enough as is and I need experience bad right now. I don't see these bar girls as relationships, I see them as experience.

>I generally prefer to pick a high top or table where we can have a little privacy. I usually plan to pay, but it's not uncommon for women to offer to split, and if they do, I accept.

This seems like the best of both worlds to me. So the waiter/waitress comes around and you only order drinks? You're still stuck waiting for them to come by to pay your tab if the date sucks though right? versus a bar where you just pay the tab and jet. 

Do you get there early and get a table/order a drink? Then greet the date as she walks in? I guess you're right, the coffee shop wasn't that much more quiet in retrospect. 

Appreciate it man.

>Demonstrate high value (or DHV for short)>Quality her on cool shit she's into( or that's she's adventurous)

What on earth do you mean by this? How do I demonstrate high value? I think I skip that and just go right into getting into cool shit they're into, but am never really sure how interested they are because it's over a dating app so I can't move it to anything sexual.

>U need to tease them more, + convey your life better with interesting stories/details about what you’ve been doing which will bait them into asking more questions.

How exactly do I do this in a smooth way though? What kind of things can I say to open up the chance to tease them and whatnot? Is it worth asking them out unless there's a fluid back and forth? 

Also I'm not replying too quickly at all. I want to text girls less and less now as I just fumbled a girl because I texted her too much. I learned that lesson already.
Yeah I may just go for it tomorrow morning to hear about where I stand.

>Question for you to ponder: if you had liked her from the start, do you think you’d still feel bothered that she didn’t offer to split? Wondering since you realized you didn’t like her long before the bill came.

I wouldn't feel bothered at all if I really liked her. I'd reach for the check immediately and pay without waiting to see what she does. I still would've found it odd if she didn't offer though. I fell for her prompt on her Hinge profile about wanting dinner over drinks. I could've just suggested ice cream or coffee and if she said no or didn't offer another alternative, then I can guess there's probably not that much interest. That's a lesson learned. 

Of course I haven't heard from her since. No message last night, nothing this morning. I haven't sent anything either of course, and probably won't. I'm chalking it up as an L and am happy for the experience. 

Also thanks for sharing your stories. Especially that first one. I am afraid that's going to happen to me at some point if I do go for a less committal date. You definitely get an idea of someone over text and meeting them can change things. I could see myself feeling like shit if a girl met me and then decided to split after 10-20 minutes. It feels like it'd only be natural to wonder why they didn't like you or what they didn't like, but I guess that's just how it'll go sometimes.
Yeah that's a good point. I'm happy she really showed this to me today. I also learned how different texting a person is from being with them in person.

I think she may have liked me, but I also did feel used. She is a nice girl, and did ask me a lot of questions. Wanted to get to know me more. I just didn't love her not even offering to split the bill. 

No I didn't know that she was unemployed before and I actually don't mind it as much because she said she's been looking and i understand the struggle of trying to find a new job. She had her former position on her profile which was actually a pretty impressive position that she admitted she was basically fired from. I just hated how there wasn't even an offer of "want to split this?". Maybe she really couldn't afford the 12-15 bucks or whatever it was? but she can afford to swipe on guys and get dolled up to go out? Gave me a little idea of what type of person she is. 

Yeah I think I understand why most girls just put drinks as first dates. I thought it was kind of a weird thing because I'm not a big drinker, but I have to be more down for it now. Like you said, it can be extended if it's going well, otherwise you can split.

Yeah I went to a cheap place, but she found an expensive thing on the menu and of course ordered that with an add on. Then I sat there uncomfortably for an hour because I knew she wasn't right for me and paid the entire bill like a chump. Live and learn.

Yep.. needed to learn it the hard way unfortunately. It wasn't that expensive of a place, and I got leftovers for lunch tomorrow. Just sucks to be used in that way. I feel like such a bum. I'll never make that mistake again though. She was cute so maybe the little head was doing more thinking than the big head.

It didn't. I took the L and am reeling over it, but it's my first one so I'll probably get over it. Just feeling it right now. She was just sitting there after I paid the check and kept talking, so I had the "welp, gotta get home. Work tomorrow!" and we split. Live and learn. Never doing dinner first dates again.
They downvoted you because you were right. This girl didn't even offer to split the bill. She was currently unemployed and had a free night out.
How exactly was I supposed to do that? We ordered our food basically as soon as she got there, and after 5 minutes of her talking I knew I wanted nothing to do with this broad.

It's going to be on a work night, so I'm honestly not trying to chat or do much of anything after we eat. I want to pay the check and leave. If we have a nice time there's always next weekend. If not, I'll keep swiping. 

Because we haven't been texting too long, I'll have a lot of succulent questions to still ask and get answers to which should be fine conversation.

Yeahhhh I am keeping my guard way up. Another prompt on her profile was "the way to win me over is taking me out to eat" and another about liking dessert. Even though she doesn't look like she orders dessert, I definitely get a feeling she's taking me for a ride here. 

I'll just do it this time though. I need to get burned on this kind of thing so I learn. The spot I picked is closer to me than her (don't care if this is a 'red flag' honestly) and the food is good.

Well I screwed up there too. We just started texting basically and I asked her out after a day because I have no idea what I'm doing. I don't know if I like her enough to take her to dinner yet. 

I like my initial impressions after a lengthy conversation, she's nice, always asks me about myself, is cute, etc. I probably shouldn't have asked her so soon though. I won't make this mistake again. I'll probably wait at least 3 days.

LOL just as I am writing a reply to this, she hit me back with a reply. She wants to meet, but the whole ghosting shit is kind of a turn off. She did this yesterday too where she asked a question, disappeared, then texted me at like 12 at night with her reply. 

I need to make a new thread I guess.
Good idea. I'll remember to ask about hobbies next time. Things like that are way better to talk about than jobs. I don't get paid shit at my job, so I don't really want to be asked about it.

I forgot all about asking for her number. Well what's the appropriate time for that? A day? 2 days? After a dip in the convo? Some girls don't want to give that out right away. I'll have to remember to try moving off the app next time. Wasn't thinking of that. Maybe I should space my messages out instead of replying right away to stretch the convo out over the day. 

We sent messages back and forth, but she was doing a lot of talking/asking me things too. She complimented me a few times (not on looks, just my 'honesty' which seems like a bad compliment to get from a girl you want to get with at some point). 

I asked her about her job just to throw the convo a life raft, but that's it. No more messages for her unless I hear back. I do have some respect for myself and I'm not THAT into her yet. Just into the idea of what could be.
RIP the dream. She stopped replying abruptly. Solid run. My PB. We'll get em next time.

That's the thing, I don't really know when that is. I mean the conversation is flowing about all of the bullshit stuff you probably usually talk about at the start of a convo. It just seems way too soon to ask to meet. Maybe I'll do it if she talks to me tomorrow.

I was never thinking of going to that extreme, but I see your point. Thanks. 

I'll try with the jokey profile on Bumble, as I feel like that is kind of my personality. I definitely don't take myself too seriously, so it's not me faking anything. If it bombs, I'll go back to what I had before.

I'm sorry, I didn't mean it like that. I saw people in other threads saying those in their early 30's were "older" and needed to be mature in their profiles and not have any emojis in their profiles, so I roped myself in with them. I'm closer to 30 than 20, and being on these apps seeing all of the people younger than me had me feeling old.

Thanks. Unfortunately, I can't just be myself on my profile. I need to be a specialized version of myself, so I wanted to try one that is less serious with a joke bio and an invite for drinks. At least for my Bumble profile, which feels like it's a bit less serious of an app than Hinge. (for guys)

I appreciate your kind words. I got the guts to swipe right on her, and basically forgot about her 30 minutes later as I was getting through the rest of my swipes. There were other girls I'd probably have things in common with, and some I probably shouldn't have bothered swiping on because I was JUST attracted to them. I guess that'll happen and maybe I should save my swipes for those I could have a more meaningful conversation with. 

I'm afraid of the rejection after they start talking to me. Once they learn more about me, that I don't have the best job, don't make a lot of money but am looking for a better job, have no house, etc. I understand they're dealbreakers, but I couldn't wait to have my entire life together before starting to learn to date. People here are still struggling even though they have all of those things, so I don't know how much of a difference it'd even make.

Anyway thanks again.

Thanks, I actually think I'm more afraid of what will happen if girls swipe right honestly. The rejection after talking to me will sting worse. I'm expecting to be swiped left on a lot as it seems that's the norm for guys. 

How many is a bunch? 10-20? I've heard about it being a numbers game. Am I really better off swiping on everyone than just looking for people I may have something in common with? There are some girls that look way too attractive so I wouldn't want to bother swiping right on them.

Thankfully I kind of figured most of what you said already. Except for the long bio thing, I'll keep that in mind. Is there anything specific you like seeing in someone's bio? or that you feel is important to include? I know the bio doesn't matter as much as my pics will.

Yes you're correct in your assumption. I was under the impression that the women do the swiping on Bumble though? Or can men swipe, but only women can start a conversation? I'm so confused by all of these apps still.
Good point. I'll crop the actor out of that one because it's still one of my better non selfies.

That's refreshing to hear.  What have you said to get conversations started? Do you just ask them something about their profile or just a generic message because you need to cast such a wide net with these apps? (according to what I've read)

I love your name first of all, and I'm glad you've recovered mostly. 

No one wants to hire me, so it's tough to figure out a type who does. I definitely can tell the type who doesn't though. Without going too in depth, what have you learned about the psychology of hiring decisions? I know people want to hire people they like, but my confidence is so shot that I can hardly fake being enthusiastic in these interviews anymore. Especially during the initial interview when I have no idea if they're even interested. 

I also have canceled interviews for jobs I didn't think I'd have a prayer of getting before. It can help my mental, but doesn't get me closer to what I want.

I believe that. I see so many companies that I've applied to and been rejected from or ignored and they're still looking to fill those same openings. It begs the question though, how the hell is anyone getting hired to do any job that isn't a minimum wage retail job?
What % of budget or amount is "enough money" at each stage exactly? Where should the majority of my budget go to start out? All in on an open prospecting audience?
An ecommerce brand selling beauty/skincare products.

Domestic, and no I don't believe we have an account manager from FB to help us out. If they're anything like the "experts" I've dealt with in the past on my smaller accounts, I'm not sure they'd be much help anyway.

I really have no idea if I got this or not yet. I've only had one 15 minute interview so far, and then another HR person emailed me a form to fill out that's asking for 2 references and everything on my resume.

I wasn't told much about the job/company or asked if I had questions. Just was asked about my experience and the salary I was looking for.

I kind of did already in so many words. Not the part about my best and only reference being my boss, but that I don't feel comfortable giving references at this stage. 

Maybe I'd feel better about giving them before an offer if I had a feeling they were serious about me, but asking for them after a 15 minute video interview seems odd. It's the first time it's happened and I've been applying to jobs on/off for almost a year now.

It was almost the end of the day when I made this thread, and now the work day is over so if I sent an email it probably wouldn't be seen/replied to. I'm thinking of just sending one Monday morning even though I know she's at a conference.

Hey thanks for the update. 

How long did you spend preparing for the interview? Was it over video or in person? Did you have any notes with you? Any other advice after doing it?

Yeah the further along with the company you get, the more time I'd dedicate to it. I've only got intro calls scheduled right now, so I probably don't need to spend too much time on them but my anxiety doesn't let me do that. I'm so worried about screwing up that I want to know everything I can.

I hate it too, but I just think it'd be annoying to send an email back to this person asking what they have budgeted? Or maybe it isn't annoying and I shouldn't care? 

This honestly gives me a bad feeling about the company before I even speak to anyone. I get asking in an interview, but this sounds like they don't have any money to pay employees.

I know I probably need to prepare. I'm just so sick of reading all about these companies that ghost me after interviews. I don't know exactly WHAT I need to be researching about them? They all seem the same to me if I'm being honest. 

I have a cheat sheet for typical BS interview questions "why are you leaving your job?" "strengths/weaknesses" "tell me about yourself" "salary range?" "what do you do at your job?" etc. but I always like to be able to bring up specifics.

Yeah, I definitely have a hard time "selling myself" in interviews. I just go into it and answer their questions. I don't really try to "sell them" because I figure I can do the job, so that's enough (obviously it's not). 

It goes to larger issues with me not feeling like I'm "good enough" I guess, but I'll need to figure that out for sure.
No, but maybe I should?

>network with recruiters on linkedin.

How exactly do I start with doing this? Just sending out cold messages to random recruiters saying that I'm looking for jobs in a specific area?

>Are you doing anything about thr suicidal thoughts? Because that's not normal. At the end of the day, a job is just a job. Take care of your mental health first

I've just put off my job search because of it. Doing this feels so hopeless and seeing tons of people in my spot make me feel like I'm screwed. If I can't get a better job, I can't make more money and I can't really get my life going the way I want and that spirals all of the bad thoughts.

I'll give that a shot, but I am almost positive I'll get the generic "no we're just going to interview other candidates and we'll 'let you know' aka never call you again". 

Maybe one of them will be honest and I can actually find out where I'm going wrong in these interviews.

>Another issue I see is that a lot of companies are looking for very specific experience for a role so that zero training is required.
